leverage.exposure: Nothing is leveraged right now — the balance is positive and no position is open. Every move recommended here would change that, and all of it has to be unwound before the matchday locks, because a negative balance at kickoff scores nothing for the entire matchday and that risk outranks every point of upside on this page. The offer that lands first takes the balance negative on its own; the sale that clears it cannot fire until that offer settles. Each flip leg added on top is another unwind to remember, and the unwinding has enough slack to be comfortable only if it is actually done. The sequence matters more than the size: offer settles, then sale, then flips closed out, all before the lock. If there is any doubt about being at the app before the deadline, take fewer legs.

verdict.detail: Hold the course, with one thing newly contested. The Makengo bid stays in — but for the first time this season a source dated TODAY argues he will not start, and that is this run's headline rather than any new trade. Weighed against his unbroken run of starts, a club injury record that formally closes the muscle issue, his absence from the live injured-and-suspended table, and the fact that the man named as displacing him is sitting unsold on the board with a collapsing market value, the preview looks like auto-generated carry-over of a note this ledger already retired. The bid is held. It cannot be improved on later information either: Freiburg's matchday-nine side is not announced until after the offer resolves, so this is the decision, taken now. Second item, measured rather than assumed: the run deliberately slept through the nightly market-value boundary and found the board completely unmoved on the far side of it, with the update marker already rolled to tomorrow. That may be nothing worse than propagation lag, but if the next run finds the same values again then tonight's tick simply did not pay, and every flip priced on the drift is mispriced. Flagged, not concluded.

sell.reason: Hwang remains the one sale, and it remains CONDITIONAL on the Makengo offer landing — not before. Selling him while the squad is twelve drops it to eleven, which forces every player to start, which forces Nakuzola in. News changes nothing in his favour and mildly strengthens the case: he is fit, so no discount is forced, but he has started only a small minority of this season's matches, and the dated trail around him at Schalke turned from praise to a public dressing-down and a clear-the-air meeting inside a week. His own ask has sat on the market unbid for days at a premium the measured clearing band says nobody in this league pays to a manager. If the Makengo offer lands, take the board price rather than keep waiting on that ask; if it lapses, keep him and keep the eleven intact.
